#2630. ‘Hard to win': Simons, Walker carry Portland lessons into Sixers roles

'Hard to win': Simons, Walker carry Portland lessons into Sixers roles originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Anfernee Simons and Jabari Walker shared the floor for 128 games in Portland. The Trail Blazers won 43 of them.

They sat beside one another in the Sixers' interview room Thursday night after a victory and discussed what the other 85 taught them.

"Whether you've got a big role or a small role, it's hard to win in the NBA," Simons said. "We've seen it firsthand."

Their roles were considerably different then.

Simons was an established starter entrusted with creating and scoring. Walker, a 2022 second-round pick, was trying to establish himself in a rotation. During their three overlapping seasons, Portland went 33-49, 21-61 and 36-46. The Blazers missed the playoffs each year.

Both are now reserves on a Sixers team constructed to contend. In nine games they've both appeared in this season, Philadelphia is 7-2.

They provided 26 points, 11 rebounds and six three-pointers in the Sixers' 123-112 win over the Raptors at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Simons scored 17 points and shot 5 for 6 from three-point range. Walker recorded nine points and eight rebounds, including four on the offensive glass.

The Sixers outscored Toronto by 24 points during Simons' 23 minutes. Neither former Blazer committed a turnover.

Their production helped Philadelphia overcome a 17-point first-quarter deficit and improve to 10-3 without LeBron James.

"You learn once you come off the bench to kind of read the game before you get in there," Simons said. "Obviously, we started off kind of slow. You just want to go in, bring some energy, get some stops, get out and run. I think everybody who got off the bench brought energy."

Simons supplied an immediate lift with a deep three-pointer at the first-quarter buzzer. His shot ended an 8-0 Sixers run and trimmed Toronto's lead to nine.

He remained involved during an 11-0 burst late in the third quarter, knocking down a three and setting up Walker for a basket. Walker then made a three early in the fourth before Simons scored on the Sixers' next possession.

When Toronto pulled within six with less than five minutes remaining, Simons answered with his fifth three-pointer.

Making those shots is the most obvious way Simons can help a roster already featuring James, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown. He said the Sixers have not made him feel as though every opportunity must go in.

"They encourage us to keep shooting the ball," Simons said. "Knowing that a team has that much confidence in us to keep shooting makes the game that much easier. Whether you miss or make, as long as we get the right shots in the right moments, I think everybody can live with the misses and makes."

Simons spent seven seasons in Portland before playing last year with Boston and Chicago. His move to Philadelphia reunited him with Walker and Rayan Rupert, another former Blazer who joined the Sixers on a two-way contract during the offseason.

Knowing familiar faces awaited him helped Simons enter another new locker room.

"It made the transition seamless," he said. "Just being able to have some comfortability with guys that I played with for multiple years. It's been fun, kind of feeling like a little bit of old times. Me, Bari and Rups have been through a lot."

Walker's path to Philadelphia began a year earlier and required an additional step.

After playing 188 games over three seasons with Portland, Walker signed a two-way contract with the Sixers in July 2025. He earned a standard contract in February and has since pushed his way into the backup-center conversation despite standing 6-foot-7.

Walker believes some of the work he did on losing teams was easily missed.

"When I first got to the league, I was part of a rebuilding process," he said. "I just felt like some of the little things I did didn't always get noticed when you're losing. I told myself, if I ever got to be part of a winning organization, then I'd go out and expand my abilities."

Rebounding has made Walker difficult for Nick Nurse to overlook.

Walker credited his timing and strong hands to lessons passed down by his father, former NBA center Samaki Walker. Those instincts have become especially useful while the Sixers piece together their frontcourt behind Embiid.

"Rebounding is a skill I kind of honed in on," Walker said. "My dad was a good rebounder. He was known for his rebounding and his timing. I think it's just a gift that he transferred to me."

Walker has made it clear that he expected to earn a role this season.

"I don't know if I was delusional, but I always felt like I was going to play and I was going to be a part," he said. "I read something where they said it's a surprise, but if you were around me this summer, it wouldn't be a surprise. This is expected, and I just want to continue to get better."

The freedom Simons once had in Portland is no longer necessary. Walker does not need a high volume of touches, either. Both understand that playing beside the Sixers' stars requires shooting when open, moving the ball and handling the less glamorous work.

"You've got to find ways to impact the game multiple ways, even if you're not scoring," Simons said. "Whether it's cutting, making the right read and pass to Joel, being the right swing pass to VJ, boxing out on defense or just being in the right position."

Their opportunities will fluctuate. Simons may take nine shots one night and only a few the next. Walker's minutes will depend on matchups and the health of Philadelphia's frontcourt.

Winning has changed what they are being asked to do. Their three years together in Portland taught them why the adjustment is worthwhile.

"You feel appreciative of the times where you go into a situation where your role might be a little bit less, but you're winning," Simons said. "That's something you can't take for granted."

#2628. Spain vs England: The tactics board - Tuchel's high press and Trafford's saves take England top in Madrid

Thomas Tuchel's England won the battle for top spot in Nations League Group A3 with a 3-2 victory over Spain at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano, finishing first on goal difference and ending the world champions' 43-match unbeaten run.

The final numbers suggest a Spanish siege. The hosts had 64% of the ball, completed 462 passes to England's 243 and took 23 shots to nine. But those figures hide two very different games. For an hour, England pressed Spain into mistakes and built a 3-0 lead. After Elliot Anderson's red card in the 63rd minute, Spain threw everything forward, and only James Trafford stood between them and a draw that would have kept them top.

Tuchel set up in a 4-2-3-1, with Declan Rice and Anderson behind Morgan Rogers, Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon, and Harry Kane leading the line. Far from sitting back, England went after Spain from the first whistle. They had 69% of the ball in the opening 11 minutes, and their high press gave Spain no time to play out from the back. In the seventh minute, England robbed the hosts as they tried to build from deep, and Kane's first-time shot flashed just wide.

The left flank was England's main route forward. According to FotMob, 46% of their attacks came down that side, where Lewis Hall acted almost as an extra winger. He whipped in a dangerous first-time cross in the ninth minute, set up a Rogers shot in the 18th and dribbled into the Spain box a minute later.

England were also far more effective with the ball at their feet. They completed 18 of their 20 dribbles and won 65% of the ground duels, with Bellingham driving at the Spain back line whenever he got the ball. Set pieces added more pressure. England's opening corner produced Bellingham's close-range effort in the second minute, and Unai Simon was forced into action again from another corner moments later.

Most importantly, England created the better chances. Their nine shots were worth 2.28 expected goals (xG), and they had five big chances to Spain's three. Kane converted a penalty in first-half stoppage time after Pau Cubarsi had brought him down, and Spain went in at the break without a single shot on target.

Luis de la Fuente also lined up in a 4-2-3-1, with Martin Zubimendi and Fabian Ruiz in midfield behind Lamine Yamal, Mikel Merino and Alex Baena, and Mikel Oyarzabal up front. Spain's plan ran through Yamal on the right, where 43% of their attacks came. That made the battle between Yamal and Hall the key contest of the night, since both teams were attacking down the same flank.

In the first half, England won that battle. Spain managed only four attempts before Anderson's red card, all of them before the interval and none on target. Their early chances came from Pedro Porro, who replaced the injured Marc Pubill in the 21st minute and went close with a header and a long-range shot.

De la Fuente's response at half-time was a triple change, with Dean Huijsen, Pedri and Fermin Lopez replacing Cubarsi, Ruiz and Merino. Yet England scored twice in the first 12 minutes of the second half. Ezri Konsa met Rice's corner with a completely free header in the 53rd minute, and four minutes later Bellingham slipped Ben White in at the back post for a third. Neither goal was down to aerial dominance. The two sides won exactly 10 aerial duels each, and England's edge came from winning the ball and moving it quickly.

The turning point came from England's own mistake. Jarell Quansah was caught on the ball in the 63rd minute, Yamal ran through on goal and Anderson pulled him back. Anderson had already committed five fouls in midfield, and this one earned him a red card. Oyarzabal converted the penalty two minutes later.

From that moment, the game belonged to Spain. They had 19 of their 23 shots after the red card, while England managed just one, Kane's blocked effort in the 74th minute. Yamal was at the centre of everything. He beat Hall more often, had five shots in the final 20 minutes and set up the second goal.

Zubimendi's injury in the 72nd minute forced De la Fuente's hand, and he sent on Nico Williams to give Spain pace on both wings. Three minutes later, Gordon lost the ball in midfield, Yamal crossed behind the England defence on the fast break and Williams finished off the inside of the post.

Tuchel's changes were all about protecting the lead. He took off Kane for Myles Lewis-Skelly in the 78th minute, leaving Gordon as the focal point, before replacing Bellingham and Gordon with Djed Spence and Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 83rd. Dan Burn came on for White in the 89th minute.

England had to defend their box, and they made 32 clearances to Spain's eight. White's last-ditch block denied Williams a certain goal in the 84th minute, and Trafford did the rest. He finished with six saves, including two big saves, and was credited with preventing 0.29 goals. The best of them came at the end, when he pushed away Fermin's shot and then tipped Aymeric Laporte's follow-up around the post. Simon, by contrast, made two saves and was 0.58 goals below what was expected from the shots he faced.

England's win was built in the first hour. Tuchel's side pressed high, attacked down the left through Hall, beat Spain on the ground and turned their chances into goals. Spain's late surge came only after the red card and two England turnovers. It was enough to make the final half-hour a siege, but not enough to beat Trafford. England finished top of the group on goal difference, and Spain's long unbeaten run ended in their own capital.

Observations after Brown-Maxey duo scores 58 points in Sixers' win without Embiid originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

They improved to 11-3 on the season with a 131-124 victory over the Pacers at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

Brown scored 31 points and Maxey posted 27.

LeBron James had 15 points and 11 assists. He passed Jason Kidd on Sunday for third in NBA history with 12,092 assists.

Pascal Siakam scored 31 points for the 5-9 Pacers.

On the first day of a back-to-back, the Sixers were down Embiid (right foot plantar fascia injury management), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pacers' injured players included Tyrese Haliburton and Andrew Nembhard.

The Sixers will face the Nets on Monday night in Brooklyn. Here are observations on their win over the Pacers:

Jabari Walker started for the first time this season, opening the game at center. He's been in the Sixers' rotation the past five games since Bona's injury.

Walker set up the Sixers' first basket, swiping a steal and then tossing the ball ahead to Maxey for a fast-break dunk. Maxey and Brown both began well and combined to score all of the Sixers' first 15 points.

Though he conceded five inches to 7-foot Pacers center Ivica Zubac, Walker was solid in his first stint. He got an early post stop on Zubac and then snatched a strong defensive rebound.

Dean Wade was next up for the Sixers at the five. He sunk a three-pointer on his first shot to give the team a 20-16 lead.

Walker ended up playing 25 minutes and posting 11 points and seven rebounds. Wade had 12 points and seven boards in 35 minutes. The Sixers' lack of healthy conventional centers remained a clear deficiency. Of course, everything should be simpler once Embiid is back in action.

The Sixers' defense did not have a sparkling start. The Pacers tallied 35 points in the first quarter and shot 62.5 percent from the field.

Brown helped the Sixers avoid a substantial deficit by draining all sorts of jumpers. He rarely appears bothered by close contests. Brown moved to 7 for 9 from the floor when he knocked down a three early in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope's triple knotted the contest up at 37-all.

Sixers head coach Nick Nurse needed to stray from his Plan A rotation when VJ Edgecombe picked up his third foul with 9:56 left in the second quarter. Labaron Philon Jr., who got a game with the G League's Delaware Blue Coats on Friday night, subbed in.

For a rookie guard, Philon has looked comfortable and confident on offense in most of his NBA appearances. He swished a long-range jumper in the second quarter and saw a floater rim out.

Brown reached the 20-point mark and put the Sixers up one with a slam assisted by James late in the second quarter.

He ran into serious foul trouble in the third quarter. Brown was whistled for his fourth foul with 9:53 left in the period for an off-arm shove on Aaron Nesmith. Wade entered and Brown exited.

The Sixers' slim lead didn't slip away. Walker nailed threes on consecutive possessions and Maxey jammed in a dunk.

Soon after, Tacko Fall came in for his first meaningful minutes as a Sixer. The 7-foot-6 two-way contract player grabbed an offensive board off a missed Edgecombe free throw, which drew one of the day's loudest cheers. With Fall on the floor, Maxey and James connected on an alley-oop that extended the Sixers' lead to 82-73.

Fall's main defensive assignment was 7-foot-1 Jay Huff. When the Sixers tried to sit in a zone, he was called for a defensive three-second violation. Whatever the scheme, most of Fall's defensive work will come around the paint. He certainly has exceptional physical traits as a rim protector and is not nimble on the perimeter.

Fall logged five scoreless third-quarter minutes and recorded three rebounds. The Sixers outscored Indiana by a point with Fall on the court. Given Fall is occupying a (two-way) roster slot and the Sixers are so depleted at center, it made sense to see a bit of what he can do outside of garbage time. While five minutes isn't enough for any grand conclusions, it's very safe to say Fall is a unique player.

The Sixers built their advantage to 102-87 with a Brown three early in the fourth quarter. They couldn't cruise to a blowout, though.

Siakam kept hurting the Sixers as a driver and had a highly efficient fourth quarter, scoring 19 points on 7-for-9 shooting. Quenton Jackson's layup trimmed Indiana's deficit to 119-115.

The Sixers ultimately held off the Pacers' push.

Caldwell-Pope canned a three, Wade threw down an and-one dunk, and James checked off his milestone assist with a late dish to Edgecombe for a layup.

#2624. Sixers, Brown have a ‘humbling' night in loss to Celtics

Sixers, Brown have a 'humbling' night in loss to Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Whatever Jaylen Brown and the Sixers dreamed up for their first matchup against the Celtics soon flew out the window on Tuesday night.

Brown was whistled for two early fouls, the Sixers fell behind and their early-season flaws were on full display in a 123-101 loss at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

"We've just got to get better," Brown said. "Tonight was humbling. We got outplayed, out-executed. So we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the next one."

Over 26 minutes, Brown had 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting and five rebounds against the team that traded him away this summer.

As for the endless dissection of his relationship with former co-star Jayson Tatum, Brown didn't have much to add Tuesday. There was no public reconciliation, no obvious on-court animosity and generally nothing to satisfy fans hoping for some kind of fireworks on that front.

"I'm just focused on doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else … to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson; he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics. They executed, they shot the hell out of the ball and they were the better team tonight."

Tatum scored 21 points, two of which came on a third-quarter slam over LeBron James. Paul George continued his fantastic start as a Celtic by dropping 36 points and draining six three-pointers.

The Celtics dominated from beyond the arc, shooting 22 for 49 (44.9 percent). The Sixers went just 11 for 37 (29.7 percent) on another night of underwhelming offense. The team sits 22nd in the NBA in offensive rating, 24th in three-point makes per game and 21st in three-point percentage.

"I think that we've got some guys that are obviously shooting much lower percentages than their last season or their career average — almost a handful of guys," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "And I don't think it's because they're shooting fallaway, totally contested ones. I think they're shots we want them to take. So I think they'll continue to take 'em and I'm pretty sure those will even out into their career averages."

Joel Embiid is at 37 percent from the floor and 4 for 33 from three-point range (12.1 percent).

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center got through an injury scare when he rolled his ankle late in the second quarter and hit a three early in the third. It was his first long-range make since the Sixers' home opener back on Oct. 22.

"It's a work in progress," Embiid said. "I think the biggest thing is just not thinking. I'm probably overthinking it. The rhythm of the game is different. I'm so used to having to create for myself, so it's a little bit different.

"But I think I'm slowly getting better. You could see as soon as I made a three, the next shot in the short corner … I didn't even think about it. I just shot it and let it fly, and I made it. … I think it's just about taking what's in front of you. Make or miss, keep working on your game. It's going to get there at some point."

Even with the Sixers second in the Eastern Conference standings at 9-3, Embiid believes the team's defense has "slacked off a little bit" in recent games.

"I don't really look at the record," he said. "I just look at the process of, 'Are we getting better every day?' We can always do a better job at all phases of the game."

"They're one of the top teams in the league and they've been together for a while," Brown said. "We've got a lot to work on over here, so we've got to get to work."

The Sixers will face the Raptors on Thursday night in Philadelphia.

They'll have to wait until Jan. 21 in Boston to see the Celtics again.

"I was looking forward to this," Brown said. "I was looking forward to playing well, but s— happens. Just get ready for the next one."

#2622. Packers Snap Counts, Week 10: Green Bay’s offense played heavy

For the second week in a row, the Green Bay Packers' reserves got on the field. Last week, it was because they were beating down the New England Patriots so much. This week, it was because the Minnesota Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times while building a three-score lead.

It wasn't a pretty game, but that's not going to stop us from breaking down the Packers' depth chart coming out of the loss to the Vikings. Below are all of the offensive and defensive snaps their players took today.

Tyrod Taylor got one drive of garbage time, a three-and-out, at the end of the game, but he's going to see more playing time soon if the team can't protect Love.

The Packers chose to make Pierre Strong Jr. a healthy scratch in this game in favor of the three backs they kept up. Together, those players ran 16 times for 56 yards on the day. Chris Brooks, who nearly played as many snaps as both Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd combined, only carried the ball twice for one yard.

At some point, you have to wonder if Brooks' blocking back role is a clear tell to opposing defenses that they're free to fire off the ball and get penetration, because the team is obviously going to pass the ball.

This might come as a surprise to many, but the Packers, who never had a lead in this game and were only tied for less than five minutes, played most of this game out of two-receiver sets. On a per-play basis, Green Bay averaged 2.2 receivers per play.

For whatever reason, the Packers must have thought that the key to beating this Vikings defense was to add more bodies into the formation to help block blitzes, rather than spreading out pass-catchers to put more stress on blitz paths.

Receivers Bo Melton and Skyy Moore both got hurt before they could even play offense. Melton went down with a thigh injury. Moore went down with an ankle injury after just being activated from the injured reserve this week. Matt LaFleur wasn't asked about either injury in his post-game press conference on Sunday.

The Packers averaged 1.8 tight end snaps per play once you include their extra offensive line looks. For perspective, tight end Tucker Kraft played every single snap on offense that Jordan Love did in this game. Every snap that Jonnu Smith and Mark Redman played was as second or third tight ends (Drake Dabney played garbage time).

Bringing an extra tight end in the formation only allowed Minnesota to bring another defender into the box, though. Eventually, you have to win one-on-ones. The Packers just weren't able to do that, as their heavy formations weren't able to punish the blitz-heavy Vikings on the ground.

Green Bay didn't sit any of their offensive linemen when Taylor went in at quarterback in this game. Mekhi Becton's snaps came as an extra tight end. The full-time offensive line was Jordan Morgan, Laken Tomlinson, John Williams, Travis Glover and Anthony Belton (left to right). Neither Jager Burton nor Aaron Banks got any snaps.

In the post-game presser, LaFleur said that the team wanted to move Tomlinson back to his "natural position" at left guard. That's why Banks (who usually played left guard) was displaced in favor of Glover in this game. LaFleur stated that Glover had more "time on task" at right guard.

It looks like we're going into the bye without any answer at right guard, as we're getting ready to ramp up another competition between Glover, Banks and Kevin Zeitler, who was inactive today after being listed as questionable with two injuries on Friday.

With both starters already out, Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper had to play the Mike and Will positions this week. McDuffie missed one snap with an injury, forcing Nick Niemann, a core special teamer, onto the field. That one play was a touchdown, where Niemann was given a lot of eye candy and let a tight end cross his face.

Brandon Cisse left the game with a rib injury but was never officially ruled out by the team, only listed as questionable. Carrington Valentine took Cisse's snaps at right cornerback for the remainder of the game.

Usually, Valentine is the team's second slot defender in their dime personnel looks, which they rarely use. Because he was forced to play on the outside, Kamal Hadden played two snaps in the slot today. One of those was a third-and-15 conversion, where he simply got beaten in man-to-man coverage.

With enough injuries, special teamers being forced into defensive roles become a problem. Hadden had played 101 special teams snaps to just 13 defensive snaps (12 of which came in garbage time blowouts against the Chicago Bears and New England Patriots) in 2026.

LaFleur was not asked about Cisse's injury in his press conference.

Slot defender Javon Bullard was only on the field for about half of the game today, as the Vikings tried to play a heavy offense that kept Bullard sidelined in favor of an extra interior defensive lineman. The slot defender rate varies a lot game-to-game because of offensive personnel and game situation, but usually the Packers play Bullard around two-thirds of the time on defense.

#2620. 5 Free Agent EDGE Rushers Lions Could Sign Following Aidan Hutchinson Injury

The Detroit Lions are 7-2, riding a five-game winning streak, and looking like legitimate Super Bowl contenders. Unfortunately, Sunday's victory over the New England Patriots in Germany came with a devastating price.

Star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson reportedly suffered a season-ending knee injury, leaving general manager Brad Holmes with one enormous problem to solve.

Hutchinson suffered the injury while celebrating a first-quarter sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. The Lions initially listed Hutchinson as questionable before ruling him out for the remainder of the game.

With the NFL trade deadline already behind them, Detroit's options for adding outside help are limited to free agency and potential practice-squad signings.

The good news? Several experienced pass rushers remain available.

According to Sharp Football Analysis' updated November 15 free-agent tracker, these five EDGE rushers are still on the market and could be worth a phone call from Holmes.

Nov 13, 2026; Munich, Germany; Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (97) at press conference at FC Bayern Campus. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Of the available options, Leonard Floyd might be the most intriguing combination of veteran experience and immediate pass-rushing ability.

The 34-year-old has played for the Chicago Bears, Los Angeles Rams, Buffalo Bills, San Francisco 49ers and Atlanta Falcons. He recorded at least nine sacks in five consecutive seasons from 2020 through 2024 before his production dropped to 3.5 sacks with Atlanta in 2025.

Floyd isn't the player he was during his prime, but he has extensive experience rushing opposing quarterbacks and could provide Detroit with a veteran rotational presence.

Interestingly, the Lions wouldn't be alone in considering him. A November 12 report from Cincy Jungle identified Floyd as a potential option for the Bengals following their unsuccessful attempt to acquire pass-rushing help.

He wouldn't replace Hutchinson's production, but Floyd could be an attractive short-term solution.

If Holmes wants to gamble on a veteran with an impressive pass-rushing résumé, Haason Reddick deserves consideration.

The 32-year-old has recorded 61.5 career sacks and previously enjoyed four consecutive double-digit sack seasons from 2020 through 2023. During his prime, Reddick was one of the NFL's most productive edge defenders.

Unfortunately, his recent production has declined considerably.

Reddick recorded just 2.5 sacks during the 2025 season with Tampa Bay, and his last two NFL stops have been disappointing compared with his earlier success.

Still, Detroit doesn't necessarily need him to play every defensive snap. A reduced role focused primarily on rushing the passer could offer an opportunity to maximize whatever Reddick has left.

The question is whether Holmes believes Reddick can rediscover enough of his previous form to make a meaningful impact.

While Floyd and Reddick bring established veteran résumés, Yetur Gross-Matos offers something different.

At 28 years old, the former Penn State standout is considerably younger than several other available options. He was selected by the Carolina Panthers in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft and later joined the San Francisco 49ers.

Gross-Matos recorded a career-high 4.5 sacks with Carolina in 2023, but injuries have limited his ability to establish himself as a consistent contributor.

He appeared in just eight regular-season games with San Francisco during the 2025 season and did not record a sack.

Despite those concerns, his size, length and experience make him a legitimate candidate for a rotational defensive end role.

If Detroit wants a player who might offer more than a short-term veteran stopgap, Gross-Matos could be worth evaluating, provided his medical situation checks out.

Clelin Ferrell hasn't lived up to expectations since the Raiders selected him fourth overall in the 2019 NFL Draft, but that doesn't mean he couldn't help Detroit.

The former Clemson standout has spent time with multiple organizations, including the Raiders, 49ers, Chargers and Dolphins.

Ferrell has experience playing defensive end in different defensive systems and could provide depth against both the run and pass.

He recorded four sacks across nine games during the 2025 season, showing that he can still contribute as part of a defensive-line rotation.

Miami released Ferrell from its practice squad in September 2026, and he remains listed among the available EDGE rushers.

For Detroit, the appeal would be adding a player with considerable NFL experience without expecting him to become the centerpiece of the pass rush.

The final name is one Lions fans should know quite well.

Preston Smith spent six seasons with the Green Bay Packers, regularly lining up against Detroit as one of the NFC North's more recognizable pass rushers.

The veteran recorded eight sacks during the 2023 season and has posted multiple double-digit sack campaigns throughout his career.

Smith, who turns 34 on November 17, last played for Washington in 2025 and remains available in free agency.

At this stage of his career, expecting him to consistently dominate opposing offensive tackles would be unrealistic. However, his experience, familiarity with NFC North opponents and ability to contribute against the run could make him a reasonable depth addition.

And considering the Lions are trying to navigate the remainder of a championship-caliber season, having another experienced veteran available certainly wouldn't hurt.

Nobody on this list is going to replace Aidan Hutchinson, and pretending otherwise would be ridiculous.

Hutchinson is one of the NFL's elite defensive players, and his absence changes how opposing offenses can attack Detroit.

Still, the Lions have already demonstrated an ability to overcome significant adversity. Following Sunday's win, Dan Campbell praised his defense for stepping up after Hutchinson went down, just as the unit previously did when Jack Campbell suffered his injury.

The question now is whether Holmes is comfortable relying entirely on the players already in the building or believes an outside addition could help Detroit maintain its defensive momentum.

Of the five available options, Leonard Floyd and Haason Reddick offer the most accomplished pass-rushing backgrounds, while Yetur Gross-Matos provides a younger alternative.

These are potential free-agent targets, not players Detroit has reportedly contacted or expressed interest in signing.

With the Lions chasing something much bigger than regular-season victories, Holmes has an important decision to make.

And this time, standing pat could be a much tougher sell.

Dominick Barlow is still dealing with the low back stress reaction that has delayed his season debut. Adem Bona is out at least for another few days with a cervical spine strain. And Hukporti is obviously out as well, barring a medical miracle in the next few hours that can instantly cure torn Achilles tendons.

Jabari Walker, who stands 6-foot-7, figures to draw the start at "center" for the Sixers. The other options at head coach Nick Nurse's disposal are 6-foot-9 forwards LeBron James and/or Dean Wade, along with two-way signee Tacko Fall.

Walker is a strong rebounder and does what he can to make up for his lack of height, but he provides almost zero rim protection. The Pacers figure to force the issue down low with Pascal Siakam and Ivica Zubac all game as long as those two can stay out of foul trouble.

Might this be our best chance yet for Tacko Time? He played three minutes in the blowout loss to Cleveland last Friday and made a brief cameo at the end of their win over the Toronto Raptors on Thursday, but that's the extent of his playing time thus far this season. Jaylen Brown, his former teammate in Boston, recently advocated for more Tacko Time, particularly given the depleted state of the Sixers' frontcourt.

Barlow appears to be on the mend, although Bona is facing a murky timetable to return. Head coach Nick Nurse told reporters earlier this week that Bona had seen a specialist for his injury and would be out for at least another week, which has effectively granted the backup 5 job to Walker by default for now.

The Sixers have little choice but to downsize against the Pacers now, which is hardly optimal against the 6-foot-8 Siakam and the 7-foot Zubac. The Pacers might have a layup line all game, although this will force the Sixers to get creative defensively. They should look at this as an opportunity to hone their small-ball looks against traditional frontcourts and figure out counterpunches if their opponent looks to just pound the ball inside.

If the Sixers do succumb to Tacko Time and give him more playing time than they have to date, that could also help them answer some questions about how they're using that roster spot. If the Pacers drag him into every offensive action, how long can Nurse stick with him before the game slips away from them? Can he hold his own and buy them some time? If not, what's the point in spending a two-way spot on him in the first place?

We're still a few weeks away from the Sixers being able to sign someone to a prorated veteran-minimum contract while staying under their first-apron hard cap. Trade winds are beginning to swirl now that the season is almost one month old, but the Sixers can't include anyone whom they signed this offseason until Dec. 15, which leaves Justin Edwards' $2.4 million contact as their best salary-matching trade bait for now.

The Sixers would likely prefer to avoid having to fill their final roster spot until they get closer to the trade deadline so they can maintain as much optionality as possible. But if Barlow and Bona don't return soon, how the Sixers fare Sunday in an Embiid-less game could help determine how imminently they need to solve their backup center issues.

Here's everything you need to know from Jacksonville's Week 10 40-23 victory over the Titans in Nashville.

Travis Hunter's diving first-quarter interception to get the ball back for the Jacksonville offense, following their turnover, was a thing of beauty and my favorite highlight, as Anthony Campanile's group continues to force turnovers inside their own 30-yard line.

#2616. Germany dominate Serbia in rain-soaked Nations League clash

Germany have made a good start to the last Nations League phase in 2026, beating Serbia 3-1 in a rain-soaked contest. Goals from Wirtz and debutant Gruda mean that Germany still have the chance to top their Nations League group.

The unusual behind-closed-doors atmosphere has seen selected groups of children under 15 admitted alongside teachers and football coaches following UEFA sanctions against Serbia for discrimination. However, the game still delivered on the entertainment front.

Jürgen Klopp's side needed just two minutes to break the deadlock, with Kai Havertz getting on the end of a corner before his attempt was deflected into the net by Srdan Babić for an own goal.

Germany doubled their advantage in the 14th minute following a brilliant, Klopp-esque pressing sequence. Aleksandar Pavlović played a superb through ball to Havertz, whose effort was denied by goalkeeper Vanja Milinković-Savić. Florian Wirtz reacted quickest to the rebound and calmly chipped the ball into the net.

Germany dominated the remainder of the first half, enjoying 75% possession and completing 94% of their passes. Their superiority continued after the break, with Brajan Gruda capping a fantastic solo run with a clinical finish in the 50th minute to make it 3-0.

Serbia responded just six minutes later. Babić made amends for his earlier own goal by reacting quickest after Stefan Gudelj's header from a free kick was saved, converting the rebound to give the hosts a lifeline.

Joshua Kimmich thought he had restored Germany's three-goal advantage shortly afterwards with a powerful low strike from the edge of the box. However, the goal was correctly ruled out due to Kai Havertz's passive offside position.

Derry Scherhant, one of Germany's standout performers under Klopp so far, had enjoyed a relatively quiet evening but came close to scoring in the 70th minute. After cutting inside from the left, his effort beat the goalkeeper but struck the woodwork.

Serbia substitute Aleksandar Mitrović also came close to scoring, but Marc-André ter Stegen stood firm to keep his effort out. Things then went from bad to worse for the hosts as Vanja Dragojevic received a straight red card for a dangerous challenge on Germany captain Joshua Kimmich, accidentally standing on his ankle.

Dragojević was not the only Serbian to leave the pitch early. Substitute Andrija Zivković also saw red after picking up two yellow cards in quick succession following an animated exchange with the referee shortly before full-time.

Klopp used the opportunity to introduce several other Bundesliga names, including Niclas Füllkrug, Felix Nmecha and Said El Mala. However, none managed to make a significant impact during their limited time on the pitch. They could get another opportunity when Germany face the Netherlands on Monday.

The match also marked a historic first for Germany, with Kimmich and Pavlović starting together as a double pivot for the first time. The partnership showed plenty of promise and could become a regular feature under Klopp.

Finally, it was also Germany's last appearance in their long-standing partnership with Adidas. Given the convincing performance, it was certainly a fitting farewell.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

Sep 24, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; General view of an Atlanta Falcons helmet during warmups prior to the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images

At one point during the CBS broadcast, color commentator J.J. Watt pointed out something about Jawaan Taylor, the Falcons' starting right tackle. #2612. Week 5 Look-Ahead: Stephen Curry and Caleb Wilson go down, and toss Jeremiah Fears the keys

By the end of Sunday's game, four weeks will have passed in the 2026-27 season. Unfortunately, we've got more injuries to key players to deal with, and there has also been a trade request. Most NBA players won't become trade-eligible until December 15, so it remains to be seen whether there's significant movement before then. Let's look at some of the key storylines from Week 4 before moving on to Week 5.

- Warriors lose Stephen Curry: After a 0-3 start, the Golden State Warriors looked nothing like a team capable of being a factor in the Western Conference. They then ripped off eight straight wins, thanks to Stephen Curry's continued greatness, rookie Yaxel Lendeborg being ready for the moment and a supporting cast offering consistent contributions. Unfortunately, the momentum came to a screeching halt during the Warriors' November 11 loss to the Rockets, as Curry suffered an oblique abdominal tear in the first quarter.

He'll be re-evaluated in a little under two weeks, but the injury could keep Curry sidelined for close to a month. The November 13 game against the Spurs was Golden State's first since Curry's injury, and it was not good. In the 123-85 defeat, Lendeborg shot 1-of-13 from the field, scoring three points, and Brandin Podziemski (eight points) wasn't much better, making two of his ten attempts. Those two will need to step up in Curry's absence, with the Warriors beginning a four-game Week 5 on Monday in New Orleans.

- Caleb Wilson injury shifts the ROY race: While the Bulls haven't started the season well, losing nine of their first 12 games, Wilson's play has been a bright spot. The rookie forward is averaging 18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.8 steals, 0.9 blocks and 2.3 three-pointers per game. Unfortunately, he fractured his right hand during the Bulls' November 11 loss to the Spurs and is expected to miss four to six weeks.

In their first game since Wilson's hand injury, the Bulls beat the Hawks in overtime on November 13. Isaac Okoro (15/3/2/1 with two three-pointers) moved into the starting lineup, while Norman Powell (33/5/2/1 with four three-pointers) and Josh Giddey (15/10/14 with three blocks and three three-pointers) had highly productive nights. Two players to watch after Wilson's injury are Matas Buzelis and Patrick Williams. The former appeared to have trouble finding his place in the Bulls' starting lineup with Wilson on the floor, while the latter has moved into the rotation after racking up DNP-CDs early in the season.

- Cade Cunningham historic night: Cunningham had a career night in the Pistons' November 12 double-overtime win over the Wizards, going off for 52 points, five rebounds, 11 assists, one steal, one block, three three-pointers and zero turnovers. Not only was this his first 50-point game, but this was also the first time since the NBA began tracking turnovers in 1977-78 that a player finished with at least 50 points, 10 assists and no turnovers.

After averaging 4.4 turnovers per game in 2024-25, Cunningham's average has decreased each of the last two seasons, down to 3.2 per game in 2026-27. His play is a big reason the Pistons enter Week 5 with an 8-4 record, good for third in the Eastern Conference.

- Dejounte Murray requests a trade: The Pelicans' roster felt awkward when the team opened training camp, due to the mixture of veterans whose long-term outlooks with the franchise were a bit cloudy and young players who needed room to figure out who they can be as potential building blocks. That led to Murray and second-year guard Jeremiah Fears starting together, and New Orleans began the season with four straight defeats.

Murray was away from the team for personal reasons in late October, and New Orleans went on a three-game win streak with Fears running the show by himself. The Pelicans went 1-4 after Murray's return, and on Thursday it was announced that his representation requested a trade. Pinning the Pelicans' struggles solely on Murray would be unfair, but it was clear something needed to change. Officially, Murray has missed the last two games with a sprained ankle, but it's difficult to envision him playing another game for the Pelicans. Not only does this boost Fears' fantasy value, but it does the same for Herb Jones, who has returned to the starting lineup.

- Paul George steals the show in Jayson Tatum/Jaylen Brown duel: Tuesday's game between the Celtics and 76ers was the first regular-season meeting between the teams since the offseason trade that sent Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia and Paul George to Boston. Of course, the main storyline was the relationship between Brown and Jayson Tatum, but PG-13 stole the show. In 30 minutes, George dropped 36 points, five rebounds, one assist and six three-pointers, shooting 14-of-22 from the field.

He did not play against Toronto the following night, but the only two games George has missed so far were for injury management. George played 78 games total in two seasons with the 76ers; if he stays relatively healthy, that would be a game-changer for the Celtics and for fantasy managers who grabbed him with a middle-round pick in drafts.

- The Lakers could be without Austin Reaves: Reaves suffered a contusion and bone bruise in his left heel during a November 11 win over the Bucks. Despite the Lakers not having played a game since, the guard was ruled out for their November 15 matchup with the Suns. The good news for the Lakers is that Quentin Grimes is available after missing the Milwaukee win with a finger injury; he could be the player asked to fill the void in the starting lineup.

Ziaire Williams, who began the season as a starter, may also see his opportunities increase after Jake LaRavia jumped ahead of him in the pecking order. The Lakers play three games in Week 5, beginning with a home back-to-back against the Hornets and Jazz on Tuesday and Wednesday. Between Reaves and Luka Dončić, fantasy managers rostering either player may not get full value because of injury or injury management.

- Franz Wagner carries a four-game streak of 30 points or more: The Magic forward has been outstanding recently, scoring at least 30 points in four straight games. In his most recent appearance, Wagner recorded 35 points, nine rebounds, 12 assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in a November 13 win over the Bucks.

While the schedule has been forgiving, with Orlando following up an overtime loss to the Warriors with wins over Sacramento, Utah and Milwaukee, that shouldn't take away from Wagner's play. And with Paolo Banchero (ankle) not due to be re-evaluated until late November, Franz has more room to take control of things offensively.

- The Celtics, Mavericks and Knicks have the busiest weekends: Boston, Dallas and New York will play games on both Saturday and Sunday to end Week 5. From an injury-management standpoint, Boston's Tatum, George, and Dallas' Kyrie Irving are the players most likely to be affected. Players like Payton Pritchard (Boston), Naji Marshall, and Zaccharie Risacher (Dallas) may find themselves in positions where they can take on more responsibility than usual.

The Knicks may have the most forgiving back-to-back of the three, as both of their games will be at home. Boston ends its west coast trip with games against the Kings (prime resting spot?) and Warriors, while Dallas hosts the Clippers on Saturday before visiting the Jazz the following day.

- Seven teams will have the weekend off: Among the teams that won't play on either Saturday or Sunday to end Week 5 are the Cavaliers, Rockets and Lakers. Due to a back-to-back, made worse by Friday's travel issues caused by the FAA, Cleveland didn't play any of its starters on Saturday against Dallas. In one of the most impressive performances of the season, the Cavs won. Tyrese Proctor recorded a triple-double, Meleek Thomas scored 20 points, Mario Hezonja scored 22 and Thomas Bryant recorded a double-double.

Kenny Atkinson's team plays games on Monday, Wednesday and Friday, so the stars will get a little more rest in a good schedule week for them. As noted above, the Lakers could also use a weekend to recuperate from recent injury issues. Each of the seven teams that don't play on Saturday or Sunday will be active on Friday, so the end of those games is when fantasy managers should move on from players who aren't considered "must-roster."

- The Trail Blazers get to play another back-to-back against the same team: After hosting the Thunder for games on Tuesday and Wednesday of Week 4, winning both, Portland begins Week 5 with games in Minnesota against the Timberwolves on Monday and Tuesday. For the Blazers, Damian Lillard played both games of the Thunder back-to-back, logging 24 minutes in a 20-point win on Tuesday and 32 in a 10-point win the following night. His ability to play back-to-backs coming off of the Achilles tendon rupture is encouraging, but the nature of the first win over Oklahoma City likely helped, as Lillard didn't play at all in the fourth quarter.

#2610. Patriots OL Will Campbell shares locker room update on QB Drake Maye

Even more painful than Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions was the New Engand Patriots losing Drake Maye to an ankle injury on the first drive of the game.

The third-year quarterback got his ankle trapped underneath the body of Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who beat Patriots offensive tackle Will Campbell to get a third-down sack. Maye limped off the field and headed to the locker rooms with trainers after the play.

Patriots coach Mike Vrabel didn't have an update on Maye's health during his postgame press conference. However, Campbell was able to speak with Maye in the locker room, and he shared the first update on the 24-year-old gunslinger, via MassLive's Mark Daniels.

"Will Campbell said he talked with Drake Maye and he's in good spirits," Daniels posted on X.

People can take Campbell's comments however they want to take them, but it's important to keep in mind that the full extent of the injury won't be known until Maye undergoes further testing.

The hope is obviously that it's something minor that could be healed up enough for Maye to return after the upcoming bye week. However, if he's forced to miss multiple weeks, it would be a major hit to the Patriots' playoff hopes.

#2609. Week 10 Snap Reactions: We’re on to 2027

The Atlanta Falcons are 3-7 after getting lit up by the Kansas City Chiefs. The offense looks worse than ever, and the defense is out of adjustments. Here are the Week 10 snap reactions.

After getting torched by the Bengals, the Falcons made A.J. Terrell captain of the game as a vote of confidence; it did not matter. Terrell got smoked by the Chiefs WR4 on a simple double move. Later, it looked like he busted his zone coverage, letting Emmitt Johnson skip into the end zone.

The cornerback is having one of the worst seasons of his career, and there's still a lot of football left. Atlanta needs to figure out its DB shuffling cause what they are currently doing isn't working.

Even Zac Robinson wasn't this bad. Rees calls plays like he's never seen a football game before. His best player on offense is an afterthought until it's too late; his screen game has benefited opposing defenses, and moving to the sideline won't fix any of these issues.

Kevin Stefanski has given Rees years to figure it out. He couldn't do it in Cleveland, and he can't do it with a fleet of top-10 picks. He is not the guy.

Pre-game, Matt Ryan said growth isn't linear and that Penix has shown he can play; he also ended the interview by saying the quarterback has to stack good performances. He's stacking bad ones. You can't miss a wide-open Drake London to start the game; slow starts will always catch up to you.

Missing Austin Hooper in the end zone was even more inexcusable. Penix is auditioning for his 5th-year option, and it isn't going well. The garbage time numbers won't save him, especially when there's an interception mixed in there.

The defense gave up an opening-drive touchdown but tightened up afterward. However, that didn't last long, as the offense couldn't give them any support. It was nice to see Harold Perkins Jr. have a great day after an early red zone mishap, but CJ Henderson picked the worst time to turn in a bad performance. The effort overall was not good enough.

Emmitt Johnson looked like Emmitt Smith, and wide receivers you've never heard of torched the defense. The unit has come undone, and Ulbrich can keep hitting shuffle on his lineup, but that isn't going to fix the systemic issues. They can't stop the run and therefore become vulnerable to the pass. Injuries have taken their toll, but this scheme needs more than talent; it needs legitimate adjustments.

The Falcons are gonna put up a united front in the presser, but the truth lies within their actions; this team is focused on the offseason. They stripped it down as much as they could, and this is the result. Players are auditioning for their 2027 roster spots, and they shouldn't be the only ones.

The Falcons have now lost three in a row and dropped to 3-7. Enjoy the bye week; it'll be your first Sunday without disappointment since October.

#2606. Vikings put Jordan Love through absolute hell in Kirk Cousins’ triumphant debut

Vikings put Jordan Love through absolute hell in Kirk Cousins' triumphant debut appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Kirk Cousins flashed back to his old Minnesota Vikings self at Lambeau Field Sunday. Jordan Love endured hell, though, in the Green Bay Packers' 30-10 loss.

Love took an astonishing eight sacks against Minnesota. He even fell on the wrong end of a brutal snap over his head during a shotgun formation for the fumble.

Love tossed a costly interception in the end zone too, with this football landing into the hands of Harrison Smith.

Minnesota wrapped up its eighth sack of Love with under seven minutes left in the third quarter. Which eventually convinced coach Matt LaFleur to sit his franchise quarterback later in the fourth quarter.

So the Vikings defense stole the thunder from Cousins' highly-anticipated Vikings return. He previously left the franchise in free agency during March 2024 offseason, accepting a massive $180 million contract with the Atlanta Falcons. Cousins, however, never lived up to his potential with Atlanta and eventually lost his starting position to Michael Penix Jr. in 2025.

Cousins eventually landed with the Las Vegas Raiders, during a time the franchise picked Fernando Mendoza as the top overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft. The Raiders eventually traded away Cousins to the Vikings before the NFL's trade deadline arrived.

Cousins hit 21-of-31 passes for 207 yards and tossed two touchdowns with one pick. Love, meanwhile, finished with 17-of-27 for 220 yards and threw just one touchdown, but sustained one pick.

Cousins praised the defense in his postgame interview with Fox. Now the Vikings moved to 7-2 overall while the Packers drop to 6-4.

#2605. Packers Winners and Losers: Week 10 vs. the Vikings

Part II of the Green Bay Packers vs. Minnesota Vikings matchup kicked off at Lambeau Field on Sunday afternoon, and it was…something. When these two teams met to open the season back in September, the Vikings embarrassed the Packers, scoring 22 unanswered points in the 4th quarter to win by 17. This time, the Packers embarrassed themselves and left with a 6-4 record after a 30-1o loss. There were no winners this week. Let's look at the worst of the worst.

I don't know how many drops WR Matthew Golden will be officially credited with, but my own eyeballs saw at least 3. On 2nd and 6, Golden had a bad drop which would've been a huge first down had he been able to hold on. On the very next play, they almost picked up the first down again, but he was unable to maintain possession before the ball hit the ground. Against a suffocating Vikings defense, the Packers have to take advantage of every moment QB Jordan Love is able to actually get the ball out, and today, they failed miserably. Golden is having a pretty stellar breakout year so far, and it's frustrating to know it'd be even better if he could stop being his own worst enemy. He finished the game with a team-high 5 catches on 9 targets for 70 yards.

TE Tucker Kraft's disappointing year got even worse on Sunday. He had no energy and looked like he didn't want to be out on the field. The Packers tried to get him involved, with Love targeting him 4 times, but he only came down with 1 catch for 19 yards. I'm not sure if he's in his own head, or just not feeling 100% after last year's torn ACL, but he is not the same TE with the killer mentality we're used to seeing. A small bright side: this fun play where he went under center and pitched the ball to Jordan Love.

The Packers drafted you to make 53-yard FGs. Try doing that sometime.

Tucker Kraft is having a down year. I think he can get back to his normal self, but in the meantime, we must deal with TE Mark Redman. After fumbling the first Packers pass of the day, I think I'd like to stop dealing with Mark Redman.

#2603. Jack Campbell in 'good spirits' after neck injury, Lions coach says in new update

Jack Campbell's road to recovery continues.

While his Detroit Lions were thousands of miles away in Germany winning in blowout fashion on Sunday, Nov. 15, the linebacker remained absent from the lineup as he recovers from a neck injury suffered during the team's Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings.

Head coach Dan Campbell was asked about Jack Campbell after the game.

"I spoke to him before we left," Dan Campbell, who is not related to Jack Campbell, said. "He is good spirits, and he continues to get better every day. I did not get into details of this trip, I just wanted him to know 'I'm still thinking about you, and just stay the course.'"

Jack Campbell issued a statement about his condition on Wednesday, Nov. 4. He said that he has movement in his lower body and was making progress towards regaining movement in his upper body.

Jack Campbell has been placed on injured reserve, the Lions announced on Nov. 7.

The linebacker announced in a statement on Nov. 4 that he has full movement in his lower body and is continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body. During the Fox broadcast of the Lions game against Patriots, play-by-play announcer Joe Davis said Campbell is expected to make a "full recovery."

Campbell remained hospitalized and was continuing to improve, according to CBS Sports' Melanie Collins on Nov. 8. Collins said on a pregame broadcast that Campbell said that while he doesn't want any tears or sympathy, he does want to get back on the field.

Campbell on Wednesday, Nov. 4, thanked his caregivers at Henry Ford Hospital in Detroit and the Detroit Lions medical staff.

Campbell announced in a statement on Nov. 4 that he has full movement in his lower body. He said he was continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body.

It was the first concrete update on Campbell's condition since the injury occurred on Sunday, Nov. 1. Prior to Campbell's statement, the team had issued more general updates, saying that preliminary results were positive.

Campbell appears to have avoided the worst fears that immediately followed his injury, as his updates indicate that he has avoided full paralysis from the neck down. Campbell said he has "full movement in my lower body" and was working to regain upper-body movement as part of his recovery.

REGGIE BROWN: Ex-Lions LB reflects on life-altering injury after Jack Campbell hospitalized

Campbell went down with a neck injury after tackling Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson.

He stayed down as the training staff and medical personnel surrounded him and a cart arrived. Campbell was loaded onto a backboard before the cart took him off the field. He was transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury after exiting the team's Week 8 win over the Vikings.

Campbell is a linebacker for the Detroit Lions.

The 26-year-old is in his fourth NFL season, all with Detroit. The Lions drafted Campbell with the 18th overall pick in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft after he starred in college for the Iowa Hawkeyes.

A native of Cedar Falls, Iowa, Campbell broke out during his junior season with the Hawkeyes, totaling 143 tackles, two interceptions, two fumble recoveries and a sack in 2021. Returning for his senior season, Campbell was named an All-American in 2022 and received the Butkus Award as the top linebacker in college football.

He also received the William V. Campbell Trophy, also known as the "academic Heisman," in 2022 for being recognized as the college football player with the best combination of academics, leadership and on-field performance.

More: Jack Campbell is a Lions team captain. Here's why his teammates love him

Campbell slid right in as a key piece of the Lions' defense after arriving in the NFL. However, he didn't officially break out until his third season. Campbell recorded 176 total tackles, three forced fumbles and five sacks en route to being named a first-team All-Pro and earning his first Pro Bowl appearance last season.

On May 21, 2026, the Lions recognized Campbell's breakout with a four-year, $81 million extension.

#2602. Fred VanVleet is Rockets unsung hero

The point guard position has undergone a radical transformation over the last decade and a half or so. Like any seismic change, it's hard to pinpoint a precise catalyst.

When Derrick Rose became the youngest MVP in NBA history in 2011, that was a watershed moment. His 7.7 assists per game were point guard-y enough, but the 25.1 points per game would have imposed a "shooting guard" label on him at any other point in league history. Rose was the new meta.

Houston Rockets fans know the change intimately. Firstly, Mike D'Antoni's decision to run the offense almost exclusively through James Harden was another critical juncture. Fast forward, and we're arguing ad nauseam about whether Kevin "I am obviously not a point guard" Porter Jr. is a point guard.

Here's what makes VanVleet postmodern: He's a throwback, in a sense. Ball security is his superpower. VanVleet facilitates in a low-risk, medium-reward way.

Yet, he's also modern. VanVleet launches pull-up threes that would make Mark Jackson blush. It's the only means he really has of bending defenses, and modern, starting-caliber point guards must bend defenses. At times, those shots can look a little bit absurd in the moment:

But in the bigger picture, they're part of what makes VanVleet so impactful.

Thanks, Brad. DataBallr has VanVleet's impact as even more positive, with a +14.1 On/Off split. I'm not sure why different outlets calculate on/off stats differently, but what matters is that the stats consistently demonstrate that VanVleet is a winner.

VanVleet's True Shooting % (TS%) is buoyed by his combined three-point volume and efficiency. He's hitting 39.5% of his 7.4 threes per game. For this Rockets team, that's priceless.

Many have suggested that Alperen Sengun would thrive if paired with a more dynamic point guard. It would be easy to point out that (again, per DatalBallr) the duo is +13.8 when they share the floor, but there are solid normative explanations for their success as well.

Just as VanVleet is not Jamal Murray, Sengun is not Nikola Jokic. He's a less natural shooter, and he's not on Jokic's level as a passer. That's not a knock: Sengun is a top-ten (and closer to five) passing big man in NBA history, but Jokic is a top-ten (and closer to five, and really closer to two or three) passer in NBA history.

But Sengun is perhaps a better ball-handler (it feels ethically necessary to note that he's a much better defender here, but it's not relevant here). That ball-handling ability makes him one of the best isolation bigs in the NBA, but some of Sengun's pick-and-roll finishing looks a lot like isolation basketball too. I've said this before, but Sengun and VanVleet run the pick-and-roll like Stockton and Malone. Often, the purpose of the set is largely to advance Sengun's position by a few inches before he starts cooking.

It's a job that, say, Kyrie Irving is overqualified for. That's not to say that outright that the Rockets shouldn't trade for him (for example, although it feels like he's the only star guard they're at all likely to acquire). There's a part of me that thinks the 2026-27 team is our best window, and more pure offensive firepower is what we need.

There's another (and ultimately, I think, stronger) part of me that thinks VanVleet's willingness and ability to let Sengun cook is what's best for his continuing development. The stats strongly suggest that VanVleet makes Sengun better, and the Rockets, in general, a better team:

That's as close to an objective truth as one could possibly find.

#2597. Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1

For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

Goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

In the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+

Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

That said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B

This is their first game against a Western Conference team. They have won their last 5 games. The Mavericks are 10th in the West. They are 2-4 on the road and 6-4 in their last 10 games. They are 4-1 against Eastern Conference teams and have lost their last 2 games.

The Mavericks made several moves in the off season, starting with hiring Masai Ujiri to replace Nico Harrison, who sealed his fate when he traded Luka Doncic for Anthony Davis. They also replaced Jason Kidd with Dusty May as coach. They added Zaccharie Risacher, Santi Aldama, Marcus Sasser, and Tarik Biberovic. They drafted Morez Johnson with the 9th pick in the draft and Sertio DeLarrea with the 25th pick. They Klay Thompson, Khris Middleton, Ryan Nembhard, Marvin Bagley III, and Dwight Powell.

After this game, the Celtics will host Orlando before a West coast trip that takes them through Denver, Sacramento, Golden State, and Washington. They then play one game at home against Atlanta before playing at San Antonio and Dallas. Then it's home against Charlotte before a game at Brooklyn. Next they have a 7 game home stand against Washington twice, Utah, Detroit, Portland, Miami and Cleveland.

After this game, Dallas will return home to host Golden State and the LA Clippers before a road trip through Utah, Denver, and Phoenix. Then they will host Boston, Orlando and Milwaukee before playing at Brooklyn and Philadelphia. Then it's one game at home against Chicago before games at Golden State and Sacramento.

Predicting the Celtics starting lineup for any game is tough. The Celtics have been changing the 5th starter on a regular basis and there is no telling who they will start from game to game. I've listed the most used starting lineup for them but it may change. I personally would like to see Baylor Scheierman start in place of Jordan Walsh. For the Mavericks, I've listed their regular starting lineup of Irving, Flagg, Martin, Washington and Gafford, although they may rest a player or two on the second night of back to back games.

At this time, the Celtics have no one on the injury report, but it's possible they may rest a player due to playing in back to back games. The Mavericks have 8 players on the injury list at this time. Tarik Biberrovic is out with right heel bursitis. Sergio DeLarrea is out with a right knee sprain. Dereck Lively II is out due to foot surgery. Max Christie is doubtful due to an ankle sprain. Santi Aldama is questionable with an ankle injury. Daniel Gafford is probable with a shoulder injury. Kyrie Irving is questionable due to knee injury management. If Kyrie is out for injury management, I would guess that Marcus Sasser gets the start in his place.
